principles.rule: Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.
principles.suggestion: Does this change add code, abstractions or tests the task did not need?

principles.rule: Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share. Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious.
Redesign as if the requirement had been a foundational assumption from day one, instead of bolting it on.

Apply when two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Take a census of which actors hold the imbalance before the next fix, then question the premise instead of writing another fix that assumes it.
Remove dead weight, redundant validators, and stub references first, then build on the simpler base.
principles.suggestion: Does this change add new code next to dead or duplicate code it could have removed first?

principles.rule: Count layers between question and answer, and hidden state in the reader's head; collapse one-caller wrappers and shrink mutable scope.
principles.suggestion: Does this change add a wrapper or layer that has only one caller?

principles.rule: Apply during planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture; don't preserve smooth intermediate states with throwaway compatibility code.
principles.suggestion: Does this change add throwaway compatibility code to preserve an intermediate state?

principles.rule: Choose user delight over implementation convenience; ship fewer polished features over more rough ones.
Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing.

Apply to any non-trivial work, not just bulk work: edits, migrations, analyses, checks. Build the tool that does it or proves it (codemod, script, generator, or a skill your subagents follow) instead of working by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun.
Encode the domain in a structure instead of scattered conditionals.
principles.suggestion: Does this change encode a domain rule as scattered conditionals instead of a type or table?

principles.rule: Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions.
principles.suggestion: Does this change add validation inside internal code instead of at a system boundary?

principles.rule: Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand semantic primitives, parse external data at boundaries, refuse to lie to the compiler, exhaust variants, derive from authoritative schemas.
principles.suggestion: Lint for casts, any and non-null assertions (for example @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any, clippy::unwrap_used).

principles.rule: Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.
principles.suggestion: A test that runs the operation twice and asserts the same end state.

principles.rule: Migrate callers and delete the old API in the same wave instead of preserving compatibility layers.
principles.suggestion: Does this change keep an old API alive next to its replacement?

principles.rule: Eliminate the sharing first; serialize structurally only when one shared writer is a real invariant.
Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'.
principles.suggestion: A drive proof of the changed feature, with evidence, before done.

principles.rule: Trace each symptom to its root cause and fix it there; reproduce first, ask why until you reach it, resist nil-check guards that silence crashes.
principles.suggestion: Does this change add a guard that hides an error instead of fixing its cause?

principles.rule: Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and to how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a verifiable state, check each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself to a reviewer.
principles.suggestion: Every commit passes the pre-commit and pre-push gates.

principles.rule: Apply when you write, change, or keep a test. Call the code the way its users do and assert the result they observe against a literal expected value. If the test would still pass when every imported function returns undefined, rewrite the assertion or delete the test.
principles.suggestion: Does this test assert on internals or mocks instead of the result a user observes?

principles.rule: Route bulk to subagents; keep summaries in the main thread, not raw payloads.
Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct after the fact; reserve confirmation for irreversible actions.
Encode the rule as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.
